clue.text: Construction put in to really annoy, perhaps

definitions.text: Construction put in to really annoy, perhaps

parts.words: Construction put in to really annoy, perhaps
parts.note: the phrase 'to really annoy' is itself an example of the grammatical construction it describes: an adverb wedged between 'to' and its verb

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately builds a grammatical structure just to irritate pedants.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates what it defines: 'really' sits between 'to' and 'annoy', the construction grammar sticklers object to.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical construction where an adverb separates 'to' from its verb, like 'to boldly go'.

clue.text: Prosperous location where many drag in benefit

indicators.note: the pieces for many and drag are placed inside the word for benefit

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or blessing
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
to tow is to drag along behind

explanation.surface: A thriving place where lots of people haul in welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'benefit' suggests state welfare payments, but here it means a blessing; 'where' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A town enjoying a sudden economic surge is a thriving, prosperous place.

clue.text: Speak of chief state

indicators.note: saying the word aloud gives a US state name of the same sound

parts.note: main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A request to talk about the leading nation or condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a state in the north-east of the USA.

clue.text: Attend to holes in trousers

indicators.note: attending to something can mean listening to it, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: breaches are gaps or holes, as in a wall

explanation.surface: Someone is told to mend the holes in a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attend to' reads as 'repair', but here it means 'listen to', making a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeches are short trousers fastened below the knee.

clue.text: Reprimand Rover?

definitions.meaning: to call someone in for a telling-off
Rover is a British car make and a classic dog's name, so a ..., signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: Telling off the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them; Rover read as a car-pet is the second sense.

clue.text: A criminal harbours assailant in winter, providing extreme comfort

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods
flu is the illness that attacks people in winter

explanation.surface: A crook shelters an attacker during the winter months, providing luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assailant in winter' sounds like a person, but it is the winter bug, FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is wealth, and the abundance of comfort that comes with it.

clue.text: Take in siblings, degree coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read upwards, so the run is backwards

parts.note: bros is short for brothers
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone adopts their brothers and sisters as a qualification comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' suits a down entry: one indicator turns the whole run of both pieces, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take something in, as a sponge soaks up water.

clue.text: "Elfin intimacy" only a part cryptic, no definition

parts.note: read as 'elf in intimacy': the word elf placed inside sex, a word for intimacy

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement

parts.note: letters taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: The clue claims a quoted phrase is only partly cryptic and needs no definition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elfin' must be split as 'elf in', so one word goes inside the other; 'cryptic' then rearranges the letters of 'only a part'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needing no definition is clear on its face, explaining itself.

clue.text: Support chambers supportive of one's nation

parts.note: a prop is a support
atria are chambers, especially of the heart

explanation.surface: A propped-up room shows patriotic loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'for one's country', a patriotic motto.

clue.text: Strong and fit for romance

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A robust and healthy suitor is ready for a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance in the old sense is a tale of legend or fiction, which a fable is.

clue.text: Great "Space Odyssey" film making comeback, seen all over the place

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the numerals read backwards

parts.note: the film is 2001: A Space Odyssey, and 2001 in Roman numerals is MMI

indicators.note: scattered all over means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A celebrated sci-fi film returns and is seen everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 2001 as Roman numerals is MMI; 'making comeback' turns it to IMM, and 'all over the place' rearranges SEEN to ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense and great are synonyms for very large.

clue.text: Succeed with strip

definitions.meaning: to remove a garment by tugging it away

explanation.surface: Someone does well at a striptease.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull off a feat is to succeed; to pull off clothes is to strip them.

clue.text: Neither you ____, flipping smooth

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: the blank completes the phrase 'Neither you nor I'

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank sentence with a swear word and a hint of ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither you' sets up the blank; 'flipping' turns NOR I round, and also reads as a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to smooth them flat.

clue.text: One over the eight, claiming mad character born gossip

indicators.note: to claim something is to take it in, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: the cox sits over the eight rowers in a rowing eight
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A tipsy person takes over a madman born to gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for a drink too many, but here it is the cox of a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is a person who talks incessantly, a gossip.

clue.text: American bit of fluff finds Aussie toilet out of order, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was known for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: bust means broken, out of order
dunny is Australian slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone finds a broken outback loo in an American dust bin.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST DUNNY with first sounds swapped gives DUST BUNNY.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a ball of fluff gathering under furniture is called this.

clue.text: Cheese dishes tender, use hash

parts.note: fond means affectionate, tender

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions for cheese meals: tender, then add the hash.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondues are dishes of melted cheese eaten with dipped bread.

clue.text: Jerk turns in tangible performance

indicators.note: the reversed jerk goes inside the word for tangible

parts.note: real means tangible

indicators.note: the word for jerk turns round, reading backwards

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A twitch spoils a concrete show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the twitch word before 'in' places it inside the word for tangible.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by a soloist.

clue.text: Tries again with tip of stake to run through

parts.note: to rehear a case in court is to try it again

indicators.note: the tip here is the end letter of the word stake

explanation.surface: Someone has another go with the point of a stake before running it through.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tip' is the last letter of stake, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play is to run through it in practice.

clue.text: Who disheartens stonemason, you might say?

indicators.note: taking out the heart means removing the middle letter

parts.note: a stonemason who carves gravestones might loosely be called a tomb maker

explanation.surface: A riddle about who removes the spirit from a stonemason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' is the definition: Tom Baker played the title role in Doctor Who. TOMBMAKER loses its middle M.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Baker played the fourth Doctor in the BBC series Doctor Who.

clue.text: Reportedly, piece easy — that's not so bright

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece and light means easy

explanation.surface: Word has it that a particular task is simple, though dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess 'piece' is a knight, which sounds like night.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-light is a dim lamp left on overnight, deliberately not bright.

clue.text: Bulb not entirely lit in climbing rock face

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the reversed rock face
in a down entry, climbing means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a crag is a steep rock face

indicators.note: not all of the word is used: its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A lamp only partly lit on a craggy climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the rock face, as suits a down clue; 'not entirely' drops the final letter of 'lit', and 'in' puts what remains inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic grows as a bulb made up of cloves.

clue.text: Behind doors that are locked, having been picked

definitions.meaning: selected for the team, read as in the side

explanation.surface: A burglar gets past locked doors once they are picked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside is slang for in prison; in side is being selected for a team.

clue.text: Warning suggests hen party?

definitions.meaning: a sign of things to come
a party of women only, so O (nil) MEN

explanation.surface: Foreboding about a bride's night out.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or warning; read as O MEN, it describes a men-free gathering.

clue.text: Good crime for source of claret

parts.note: rape is a serious crime

explanation.surface: A virtuous crime lies behind the red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, made from the grape.

clue.text: Forces which turn into doubt or questions

indicators.note: the word is found lying inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something casting things into doubt or raising questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Torques are twisting forces that cause rotation.

clue.text: Bar about a quarter, up to date

indicators.note: about can mean around in any direction, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
east is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A pub about a quarter full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately', but it rearranges the letters of 'Bar'; the compass point follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep abreast of news is to stay up to date with it.

clue.text: Vindication for reversible gesture

definitions.meaning: read as V-indication: the letter V followed by indication, a sign
a two-finger gesture whose meaning depends on which way the palm faces

explanation.surface: Justification for a rude hand signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-fingered gesture means victory palm out and is rude palm in, so it is reversible.

clue.text: Make yourself scarce, when badly appraised

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out wrong

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Leave when given a poor assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: To make yourself scarce is to vanish or go away.
